messages:
mira: thinking out loud — we should try a very small "rollback oracle" that lives in the router and makes per-cohort safety calls. not a full-blown arbiter, just a local decision surface + policy cache.

sam: love the minimal approach. main concerns: signal quality (false positives) and cross-cohort consistency.

alina: can you sketch the input signals? what would the router actually evaluate?

mira: initial signals: 1) 5m success-rate vs baseline (requests with 200 vs errors), 2) p95 latency delta, 3) small eval set regression alert (binary), 4) infra errors (OOM, timeouts). weighted sum -> threshold. keep it readable and tweakable.

kevin: we need hysteresis to avoid flipflop. min evaluation window 3m and a cool-down of 10m before re-enabling. also cap intensity (only drop up to X% traffic per step).

leo: what about coupling with rollout controller? router-only decisions can diverge from the global rollout state.

mira: good point. plan: router oracle can initiate a local partial fallback for affected cohort and emit an event to the rollout controller. controller can then confirm and optionally promote a global rollback. so fast local mitigation + centralized adjudication.

sam: how do we prevent noisy signals from noisy tenants? per-tenant baselines?

alina: per-tenant baselines are ideal but expensive. suggestion: two-tier baseline: global model baseline + recent-cohort baseline. require both checks to trigger for a hard rollback. single-signal triggers only a soft fallback (e.g., route to 50% fallback variant).

mira: exactly. soft vs hard actions: soft = shift X% traffic to fallback variant, keep canary live; hard = drain canary and mark for controller review. soft actions auto-reverse after window if signals clear.

kevin: propose decision surface expressed as a tiny DSL in a config map so product teams can tune without code:
```
when (success_drop > 4% and p95_delta > 200ms) or eval_fail == true -> soft_fallback(50%)
when (success_drop > 8% or infra_errors > 3) -> hard_fallback
```

leo: config DSL is neat. need guardrails: only apply soft_fallback if canary traffic > 1rps to avoid noise.

alina: telemetry — we must attach a trace/span to every router decision and emit metrics: decision_reason, action, cohort_id, baseline_snapshot. observability is critical so SREs can audit.

sre-ops: +1 on traces. also require a safety label so human oncall can override a router decision for a given cohort.

mira: override API planned. also will add a backoff multiplier when consecutive soft_fallbacks occur.

sam: any thoughts about experiment systems (A-B) vs canary semantics? experiments want to preserve treatment fidelity. automatic fallback could bias evals.

mira: we'll add an opt-in flag per experiment: auto-mitigate=true/false. default true for production rollouts, false for pure experiments. experiments maintain canonical splits unless opted in.

leo: what about rollout speed? add max_traffic_change_per_min to config to slow aggressive mitigation and give time for controller to react.

kevin: failure modes: 1) false rollback on transient upstream flakiness, 2) widespread simultaneous soft_fallbacks causing capacity issues on fallback path. mitigation: bulkhead fallback pools, and a global throttler that rate-limits aggregated fallback traffic.

mira: good. I'll draft an RFC with diagrams: router decision flow, events to controller, DSL examples, telemetry names, and opt-in flags. ask: anyone object to me prototyping the router oracle as a feature flag behind a sampler for one week?

sam: +1 for prototype. start with low-risk tenant cohort (internal infra traffic).

alina: +1. I'll own the telemetry spec.

kevin: +1, I'll add hysteresis knobs and safe defaults.

deploy-bot: deploy 1763330015: feature-flag/router-oracle-proto -> canary succeeded :rocket:

sre-ops: watching metrics dashboard. please include a synthetic probe for the eval set so we get a deterministic signal.

mira: noted. thanks everyone — I'll open the RFC and link back here.
